items.title: China or the U.S.? Two Meetings Offer Competing Showcases of Global Power.
items.summary: As Xi Jinping gathered with the leaders of Russia and Iran, Europe challenged the Trump administration at the G20, offering a split-screen view of a changing world.

items.title: The Ritual of Coffin Making in a City Hit by Ebola
items.summary: While several coffin makers in Bunia said they were providing a public service, the virus has put them at the center of a debate around safe burials.

items.title: China Censors and Punishes to Shape Narrative on Floods in Tibet, a Contrast to Nepal
items.summary: While journalists can report freely on grief and anger in Nepal, China’s official media have presented a sanitized disaster aftermath in Tibet.

items.title: U.S. Sanctions on Iran Cut Off Students From Tests Needed for Study Abroad
items.summary: The latest measures have forced the cancellation of English proficiency and graduate exams, isolating many Iranians most eager to foster ties with the world.

items.title: Weeks After Failed Drone Attack, Germany Points Finger at Russia
items.summary: The country said Moscow was behind an explosive-laden drone found near a Ukrainian plane at a German airport last month. President Vladimir Putin of Russia called the accusation “a grave mistake.”

items.title: Nepal’s Economy Has Few Ways to Absorb the Cost of Flood Damage
items.summary: The country’s government estimates that the recent catastrophic floods caused $5 billion in damage. That’s one-tenth of Nepal’s entire economy.

items.title: Israeli Raid in Gaza Kills 4, Palestinian Officials Say
items.summary: Israel said it seized the head of Hamas’s internal security force in the deadly operation. Fighting has continued in the enclave despite a U.S.-backed truce.

items.title: Can Ancient Ruins Be Protected From Wildfires? Greece Is Trying.
items.summary: As blazes surge across Europe, the country is making a trade-off to protect its heritage by fireproofing sites at the risk of spoiling the surrounding landscape.

items.title: These Ukrainian Children Go to School Underground. They’re the Lucky Ones.
items.summary: In a frontline city, parents don’t see schools built below ground as apocalyptic. Instead, they offer relief from worry about the threat of Russian strikes.

items.title: Carney Tells Trump Officials to ‘Stop Throwing Shade’ Over Canada-U.S. Trade Talks
items.summary: Amid a trade war, Canada’s Liberals swept three special votes and new polling suggested strong support for Prime Minister Mark Carney and his retaliatory tariffs against the U.S.

items.title: Bill Simmons’s Co-Hosts Are Tired of His A.I. Antics
items.summary: The founder of The Ringer is taking flak for using artificial intelligence to conjure opinions from the deceased film critic Roger Ebert. Ads from OpenAI have recently run on the show.

items.title: What to Know About Venezuelan Energy Following Trump’s Oil Deal
items.summary: The Trump administration’s deal with a private oil company to increase oil production in the South American country could take many years to come to fruition.

items.title: Two More Oil Tankers Are Attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The ships were hit near Oman on Monday, the latest attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf. Oil prices rose more than 2 percent.

items.title: At G20 Meeting, Scott Bessent Accuses China of Flooding the World With Cheap Exports
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused China for flooding the world with its cheap exports.

items.title: Ozempic Maker Novo Nordisk’s Investors Are Nervously Looking Into the Future
items.summary: Novo Nordisk’s chief executive, Mike Doustdar, is a year into a corporate turnaround. He says investors are still underestimating the promise of the company’s drugs.

items.title: Satsuki Katayama, the Woman at the Center of Japan’s Currency Fight
items.summary: Japan’s finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, is under pressure to strengthen the yen while balancing competing demands from the prime minister and Washington.

items.title: Bond Sell-Off Threatens to Squeeze Borrowers Around the World
items.summary: Government bond yields are hitting multi-decade highs, reflecting anxiety about debt levels, deficits and inflation. The effects will extend to mortgages, business loans and other types of credit.

items.title: How the Pentagon Is Getting Into the Venezuelan Oil Business Under Trump
items.summary: The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital, founded by the Biden administration to give loans to bolster the U.S. defense industry, is helping lead President Trump’s oil deal.

items.title: Shein’s Lackluster Debut Shows a Fast-Fashion Model Left Behind
items.summary: Squeezed by new trade rules, shrinking market share and labor concerns, Shein’s share decline in Hong Kong on Tuesday is a sign investors have moved on.

items.title: Donald Trump Jr.’s Firm Leads $1 Billion Funding Round for Polymarket

items.title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
items.summary: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.

items.title: Meta Shifts the Blame + Do Data Center Bans Work? + The Final HatGPT
items.summary: Meta negotiated an unusual provision in their landmark settlement: If TikTok and YouTube also agree to penalties and changes to their products, Meta will pay more.
